properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/10/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 987672
Permit API: 015-23717
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/10/2023
Comments: On 3/10/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Floydie well site. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected from water puddles on the south corner and northeast side of the Floydie well site. During an inspection on 1/24/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on two areas of the well pad surface outside of containment. In the first area, the fluid covered a 6' x 10' area and field tested at 11.93 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-039 for laboratory analysis from location N 41.665131 W -76.126503. In the second area, the fluid covered a 10' x 10' area and field tested at 4.90 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. This water puddle was in a larger muddy 35' x 20' area that field tested at over 4.0 mS conductance with a Hanna Groline meter. The department collected water sample #9551-040 from location N 41.66589 W -76.12645.On 2/25/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and lithium and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample reports are displayed in pictures 1, 2, 3 and 4.Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection however the potential for accelerated E and S exists due to the bare soils observed during this inspection. The two taken in the former location of the brine tank read 0.89mS and 1.10mS respectively. A background reading was taken and read 0.20mS. This location is displaying distressed vegetation with sparse coverage. The Department requested additional information because it has not yet been received. 1. What was released?2. When the release occurred?3. How long was the release occurring?4. Why the release occurred?5. The quantity of the release and how the quantity was determined?Based on observations from this inspection, the site appears to be unchanged since the date of IR 3477153. Therefore, violations related to the brine discharge discovered during IR 3400883 and 3482056 shall remain outstanding.

Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 855877
Permit API: 131-20219
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-07-17
Comments: I am generating this "Administrative" inspection as a follow up to inspections performed by OGI, Eric Miller on 7/15/19. Noted in remarks section of those inspections was: "Review of previous site history indicates that previous violations of 78a.86 were cited for (2) wells on pad on 5/10/13. Accessible site history did not clarify which wells were cited. Will perform internal file review to clarify which wells were cited and what actions were taken." - Internal file review revealed that previous violations of 78a.86 originally cited on 5/10/13 were for the the Yarasavage 4H and Yarasavage / Solanick 3H wells on pad. Gas was detected in the 13 3/8"x 9 5/8", (13x9) cemented annuli. The Dept. requested a response from Operator, in writing, by 6/21/13 explaining how Operator plans to comply with 78a.86. Further review of well files could not locate any documentation that the Dept. received requested response from Operator at that time. - In an effort to confirm the sustained presence of gas within these (2) wells cemented annulus, the Dept. requests that these well cellars have gravel removed to visually confirm the status of the (13x9) annuli. Following annuli status confirmation, well cellars can be filled with water so water level is above casing tops to check for bubbling. If any bubbling is noted, water level can be pumped down to confirm source of bubbling. - In the event initial testing confirms the sustained presence of gas within these cemented annuli, further assessments may be warranted, i.e shut in pressure build up tests, etc. - Please contact me when these retests can be arranged and / or with any further questions you may have. Violation ID: 897037
Permit API: 065-24137
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Perry Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/15/2020
Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of South Enterline Road in July 1997. Violations were issued during the previous inspection due to a spill from a hole in the bottom of the brine tank. Since that initial inspection, work has been started associated with the cleanup of the site. The brine tank has been removed, and contaminated soil has been excavated from the area of the spill. This contaminated soil has been placed on plastic and protected from the weather and remains on site near the wellhead. Conductivity readings taken during this inspection indicate that a small area of contaminated soil remains to be removed upslope from the current excavation area. When the remaining contaminated soil has been removed, fresh topsoil should be used to fill in this area, and mulch should be used to stabilize the area for the winter. Seed will then be needed in the spring. After evaluating the site this morning with Wilbur Carney and Brian Stanford of DE LTD, a determination was made that the spill volume appears to be less than one barrel of produced fluid. This site should be remediated as a visual cleanup.

Violation ID: 939568
Permit API: 131-20563
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2021
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 5th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-17
Comments: On 12/16/18 at approximately 0715 a water truck at the site rolled off the access road, causing an impaired water release. According to Oil & Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck's Emergency Response Team report, approximately 110 barrels of produced fluid and approximately 100-130 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. EQT reported the release to the Department at 0745. On 12/17/18 at approximately 1050 hours I conducted an incident response inspection. I met with David Guidas of EQT who explained that a water truck was on its way to the AST with a load of impaired water when it got too close to the edge of the access road and rolled over the edge onto water lines servicing the AST and frack. The spill occurred in a sediment trap, limiting the extent of the spill. Due to the presence of rain water in the sediment trap the spill impacted Waters of the Commonwealth. Approximately 90 barrels of rain water, impaired water, and diesel fuel were recovered by a vac truck. SPSI had conducted remediation of the spill at the time of investigation. Guidas indicated additional screenings were to be conducted and further excavation, as water with elevated conductivity was still being observed. Guidas indicated once the final remediation was complete Corey Giles of EQT would be handling the Act 2 process. OGIS Sabocheck indicated in his ERT report that EQT agreed to pressure test the lines prior to placing the damaged lines back in use. At the time of inspection David Guidas of EQT indicated a section of line had been replaced.

Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.

Comments: On October 3, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and WQS Samuel Steingrabe. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3343707 where violations were outstanding due to deteriorated production fluid tanks that were discharging onto the ground, a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans. Also, no production reports have been submitted since 2014 per Department database. The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photos 2 and 3). No Emergency Response plans, or other required postings were onsite. The production fluid tanks onsite appear to have been replaced since IR 3343707 (see photos 5 and 15). Soil conductivity readings were taken underneath and around these tanks to determine whether petroleum products and/or production fluids were still present in the soil since IR 3343707. These readings were taken underneath the production fluid tank valves and in bare spots in their surrounding earthen berms. An additional reading was taken in a wet spot next to the tank farthest from the site entrance. The reading taken underneath the valve of the tank closest to the site entrance read 100 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken in the surrounding berm read 111 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). The soil conductivity reading taken underneath the valve of the tank farthest from the site entrance read 380 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. All other violations shall remain open as well since the rest of the site remains unchanged since IR 3343707.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/26/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Seneca's Covington Pad R well site in Covington Township, Tioga County on 06/26/2023 at 0950. The weather was 75 degrees with overcast skies. Hydraulic stimulation activities were taking place onsite at the time of inspection. Seneca safety personnel Tighe Truman was onsite at the time of inspection.On 6/25/2023 at 0100 hours Tighe Truman of Seneca Resources notified the DEP that "Beimel Trucking was off-loading to tanks when pop-off relief valve failed spilling approximately 10 gallons of produced water to gravel. Vac truck used to recover liquid; impacted gravel scraped up and placed in bucket." The resulting spray of production fluid in front of the sites temporary storage tank offload area was estimated to be 10 gallons and encompassed roughly a 15 ft span in front of the offload area (picture 4). Steps were then taken to immediately clean the spill involving vacuuming the fluid on the pad surface and than removing impacted and stained materials from this area and storing them within the secondary containment of the temporary storage tanks until proper disposal (picture 5). The six wells onsite were undergoing hydraulic fracturing activities. Lined timber mats remain in place for the hydraulic fracturing operations. Temporary storage tanks were labeled and placed within secondary containment onsite. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the site. Straw, Erosion Control Blanket (ECB), and silt sock remain in place around the pad site. Areas surrounding the pad remain stabilized as they establish vegetation. Post- Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls remain in place. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation leaving the site was observed at the time of inspection. Based on the findings of this inspection and Seneca's timely remediation of this release, violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) are cited as immediately corrected against API # 117-22164. The DEP departed the site at 1150.

The weather was 75 degrees with overcast skies. Hydraulic stimulation activities were taking place onsite at the time of inspection. Seneca safety personnel Tighe Truman was onsite at the time of inspection.On 6/25/2023 at 0100 hours Tighe Truman of Seneca Resources notified the DEP that "Beimel Trucking was off-loading to tanks when pop-off relief valve failed spilling approximately 10 gallons of produced water to gravel. Vac truck used to recover liquid; impacted gravel scraped up and placed in bucket." The resulting spray of production fluid in front of the sites temporary storage tank offload area was estimated to be 10 gallons and encompassed roughly a 15 ft span in front of the offload area (picture 4). Steps were then taken to immediately clean the spill involving vacuuming the fluid on the pad surface and than removing impacted and stained materials from this area and storing them within the secondary containment of the temporary storage tanks until proper disposal (picture 5). The six wells onsite were undergoing hydraulic fracturing activities. Lined timber mats remain in place for the hydraulic fracturing operations. Temporary storage tanks were labeled and placed within secondary containment onsite. An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the site. Straw, Erosion Control Blanket (ECB), and silt sock remain in place around the pad site. Areas surrounding the pad remain stabilized as they establish vegetation. Post- Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls remain in place. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation leaving the site was observed at the time of inspection. Based on the findings of this inspection and Seneca's timely remediation of this release, violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) are cited as immediately corrected against API # 117-22164. The DEP departed the site at 1150.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/02/2026 to SCORPIO ENERGY INC in Howe Township, Forest county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/02/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8287770
Permit API: 053-31161
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: This site is undergoing construction for the development of a conventional well. The drilling permit and E and S Plan are posted at the entrance of the location. There was no activity on the location at the time of this inspection. The template for the site and access road has been completed. The gathering lines for this well have been buried within the template of the road. Stone has not yet been applied to any portion of the road or well site. The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well. This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. There are no apparent surface issues on the location location or the spur road leading to it.A tank battery located along FR 370 approximately 250 feet northwest of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks (11883 and 11884) within an earthen containment. There is evidence of repeated discharges of production water inside of the containment from each tank. Soil specific conductance (SPC) readings upwards of 15,000 uS/cm were detected at/downslope of the drains located on the back side of each tank. Elevated SPC is prevalent across the ground inside of the containment downslope of the tanks. Accumulated fluid pooled along the western wall of the containment has an SPC over 20,000 uS/cm. There was no active discharge at time of inspection.The fluids released inside of the containment have seeped through the northern corner of the earthen containment wall (or there is a buried drain) at 41.99216N / 78.76119 W. There is an approximate 25' x 3' area of stained soil with elevated SPC (upwards of 818 uS/cm vs 40 uS/cm of nearby uncontaminated soil) present outside of the containment's northern corner. The end of the apparent contaminated soil is located approximately 75 feet from Yeager Brook.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery containment to contain fluid inside of it will also nee to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Unconventional Y

Inspection Type Complaint Inspection

Comments Inspection conducted in response to spill reported to the Department by Chief Oil & Gas, LLC (Spill Notification ID No. 323649). Chief reported that approximately 20 gallons of brine leaked during the replacement of a produced water tank to the ground surface. The spilled fluid was immediately removed with a vacuum truck and the affected pad substrate was excavated and removed. New gravel was put in place. Mitigation efforts had been completed at the time of my inspection. New gravel was evident at the location of the spill. No odor or staining that could indicate residual contamination was noted. Because the brine spilled on the pad surface, this release had the potential to pollute waters of the Commonwealth, which is in violation of 35 P.S. § 691.402(b). Title 35 P.S. § 691.402(b) prohibits conducting activities regulated by permits issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution contrary to the issued permits or without a permit. Further, since the spill occurred off of containment during removal of the produced water tank this release is in violation of 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), which requires permittees to take measures to contain pollutants. Since actions were taken to promptly remove the released fluids from the well pad surface and remove and replace the affected pad substrate, the violations cited above are considered immediately corrected.

Stabilization added to open soil areas (Photos 1-3).The fuel tank onsite appeared to be leaking. Staining was noted on the gravel. Fuel was noted on piping (Photos 4-6).Staining at the base of the tank was noted within the gravel. No elevated conductivity was noted, however a strong odor was noted within the material. I contacted the operator and they informed me that the tank was broken upon receipt, however it was fixed. The material was from the compressor and was most like a hydrocarbon (Photos 7-10). I was unclear if this material was within the soils outside the berm as well. Staining was noted on the gravel along the access road (Photos 11-12).Gravel was added to the access road. the soil pile along the access road was removed and the area stabilized (Photos 13, 14).Diversion channels were dug along the access road, leading to the roadside channel. The channel was cleaned up (Photos 15-17).The culvert inlet within the roadside channel was displaying some accumulated sediment. I recommend stabilizing the channel to avoid access sediment from reaching the culvert inlet (Photos 18, 19).Stone was added to the lower section of the roadside channel. The channel leads to a PennDOT inlet. The bank along the channel was stabilized (Photos 20-22).The violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a) issued on 02/14/2024 for the oil/grease on the ground are being closed. New violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(a) are being issued for the fluid near the tank and the fuel on the ground from the fuel tank and failure to report.a

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/29/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/29/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 949517
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/29/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator that an estimated 20 barrels of a fresh water and produced water mixture had been released to the surface of Pad B on the same day, 3/29/22. I met with EQT representative Rick Hall upon arriving on location. Mr. Hall stated that a frac tank had been overflowed with the produced water and fresh water mixture. He said the fluid had made its way outside of the secondary containment and into the travel lane and ditch along the southwest pad edge. There is a brush barrier alongside the ditch at the edge of the pad. No fluid was observed on the opposite side of the brush barrier. I took several electrical conductivity (EC) readings of the fluid on the pad surface and in the mud in the ditch. With the Oakton conductivity meter I measured an EC of >19.99 on the pad surface immediately next to the edge of the containment where the frac tanks are located. In the middle of the travel lane, I measured an EC of approximately 16 mS/cm. The mud in the ditch at the pad edge gave me an EC reading of approximately 14 mS/cm. Excavators were present on the pad in addition to roll-off boxes to contain excavated material. A Tobias construction crew began to excavate the affected pad material during this inspection. A Creston Environmental employee was also present conducting screening on the pad surface with a YSI meter. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for the release on Pad B due to the estimated volume of the release. The Department requests a justification for the estimated spill volume. Violations noted.

Comments: Administrative inspection in response to a release reported by the Operator on May 13, 2020. Mr. hardy reported that approximately 50 gallons of production fluid was released to the ground at the Vivian Harbison Well Pad in Nottingham Township, Washington County.
